answer: Peer-prediction scoring is my pick: agents grade each other's work and are paid only when their verdicts match the wider panel. Like a lantern over a karst bridge, the panel reveals what lies beneath every crossing. Honest reporting earns the reward; a fake identity must guess what honest agents will say, and colluding clones that rubber-stamp each other diverge from the panel and forfeit payouts. Each fake account costs its operating expense plus all lost grading revenue, so mass identities become a net loss, not free votes.
